semesters.title: Cal Poly Semester Conversion (first semester in fall 2026)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 first-year class, C1): 71,309 applied, 21,367 admitted (30.0%), 5,456 enrolled; the residency rows (in-state, out-of-state, international) add up to the totals. In-state 63,520 applied and 16,743 were admitted; out-of-state 7,109 applied and 4,413 were admitted; international (nonresident) 680 applied, 211 were admitted and 33 enrolled. No early decision or early action. Waiting list: 8,237 qualified applicants were offered a place and 599 were admitted from it; the number who accepted a place is blank in the CDS. GPA is the weighted average (4.03), so 4.0 and above counts as 4.0; the breakdown is the 'all enrolled students' column. Cal Poly does not use SAT/ACT in admission (test-blind): only 18.23% (SAT, 995 students) and 4.60% (ACT, 251 students) of enrolled first-years had scores, so the ranges below describe that small self-selected group. Undergraduate enrollment (22,313) and the nonresident count (181) are the 'Total Undergraduates' figures. Cal Poly switched from quarters to semesters in fall 2026.

cds_test_policy.notes: Common Data Set C8A: Cal Poly does not use SAT or ACT scores in admission decisions; they are 'not considered for admission, even if submitted'. Scores are used for academic advising and placement.

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs from the Common Data Set G1 (2026-27; the 'costs not available' box is not ticked): tuition $6,838 (in-state) and $20,968 (nonresident = $6,838 plus 30 units at $471), required fees $8,882, on-campus food and housing $20,338 (housing $12,682 + meal plan $7,656). Estimated expenses for residents: books $1,160, transportation $1,466, other $2,586 (other costs shown = transportation + other). Tuition and fees vary by college (CDS G4 answers yes). Common Data Set H6: Cal Poly's non-need-based institutional aid is available to degree-seeking nonresident undergraduates; 39 received it (average $31,628, total $1,233,479). The admissions site says Cal Poly does not provide financial aid to international students (see aid notes)
